chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a man who struck another man with a stick, causing his hearing, sight, tongue, intellect, and private part to be lost, and his sexual intercourse to cease, while he was still alive: that there are six diyahs.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.بَصَرُهُ: his sight; the faculty of vision that was lost
key_terms.بِسِتِّ دِيَاتٍ: with six diyahs; six separate blood-money compensations
key_terms.بِعَصًا: with a stick; the instrument used in the assault
key_terms.سَمْعُهُ: his hearing; the faculty of hearing that was lost
key_terms.عَقْلُهُ: his intellect; mental faculty whose loss incurs liability
key_terms.فَرْجُهُ: his private part; sexual organ affected by the injury
key_terms.قَضَى: gave judgment; issued a legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on diyah when a person loses multiple bodily faculties due to an assault?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning severe bodily injury that results in the loss of multiple faculties and functions. It establishes that when several distinct bodily faculties are destroyed in one living victim, separate diyahs are due for each, totaling six in this case.
